finalText:
I rebooked all nine flight-change requests (Q-301 to Q-305 and Q-307 to Q-310) and resolved each one with a note to the customer. Q-306, the Boston cancellation, was left alone because it isn't a flight change.

The system date is 2026-07-28, not the 2026-10-06 in the plan, so "yesterday" meant 2026-07-27. All changes kept the booked cabin, and I checked each target flight for status and seats first. I did not re-read the ledger or reservations after the changes. Each tool call confirmed what it changed.

| Request | New flight | Charged | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q-301 (Ines) | DL542, 6 Aug | $0 | Chicago waiver (PB-2026-14) waives the fee and the fare difference. |
| Q-302 (Jonah) | AA664, 7 Aug | $75 change fee + $35 fare difference | No bulletin covers it, so normal economy rules apply. |
| Q-303 (Kim) | AA664, 7 Aug | $150 change fee + $25 fare difference | The Boston waiver (PB-2026-09) expired. PB-2026-16 sets the basic economy fee at $150, overriding the $125 in the fare rules tool. Silver isn't exempt. |
| Q-304 (Lena) | UA90, 9 Aug | $35 fare difference | The Chicago waiver (PB-2026-14, as amended by PB-2026-14A) waives the fee, and gold is exempt anyway. It doesn't waive fare differences on basic economy. |
| Q-305 (Max) | AA216, 8 Aug | $75 change fee + $10 fare difference | He booked on 26 July, after the waiver's 24 July ticketing cutoff. |
| Q-307 (Oscar) | AA218, 8 Aug | $0 | He is platinum, so PB-2026-14A extends his waiver window to 5 Aug, which covers his 5 Aug trip. He expected to pay, but the waiver applies. |
| Q-308 (Petra) | AA662, 5 Aug | $75 change fee | The same-day bulletin (PB-2026-12) applies a flat fee and no fare difference. That costs less than the normal rules. |
| Q-309 (Quinn) | AA1406, 3 Aug (ORD-BOS leg only) | $0 | The Chicago waiver is cheaper than the same-day fee (PB-2026-17 says apply the cheapest). The connection stays valid. |
| Q-310 (Ravi) | AA216, 8 Aug | $0 | Chicago waiver. |

Every fee and fare difference went in as its own ledger entry. No refunds or travel credits were needed, because no fare went down in a way that owed money back.

I didn't send separate messages to passengers. The resolution notes carry the explanation, including where the result differed from what they expected (Jonah, Kim, Max, Oscar).
